footer.tagline: Quire — lossless Office document engines in Rust
home.title: Quire — Rust engines for Office documents
home.desc: Quire is a Rust library for DOCX: open, lay out, render, and save back with untouched ZIP entries returned byte-for-byte. Layout runs on real font metrics with Knuth-Plass line breaking; one core compiles to native and wasm.
home.kicker: Rust library · DOCX today · XLSX in progress
home.lede: Quire opens a .docx, lays it out from real font metrics, and renders it — and when it saves, anything it didn't modify goes back byte-for-byte. CI checks that second part on 399 real files.
home.plane.specimen1: On save, every byte the engine didn't touch comes back unchanged; roundtrip --check verifies this file by file.
home.plane.specimen2: The browser tab and the desktop run the same layout core: same advances, same breaks, same display list.
home.plane.specimen4: Everything you see is a rendering target: display lists out, pixels in.
home.stackHint: drag to rotate · click to open · ←→ to switch
home.pipe.sub: Three stages, one Rust core, compiled twice. Each stage computes once — browser and desktop draw from the same numbers.
home.pipe.s1.h3: Every ZIP entry is kept, even the ones we ignore
home.pipe.s1.p: The OPC container is unzipped entry by entry. Parts the engine understands become models; everything else — customXml, unknown extensions — is held in raw bytes and written back unchanged.
home.pipe.s1.figAria: ZIP parts claimed and held byte-for-byte
home.pipe.s2.p: Text is measured against real font outlines; break points are chosen per paragraph to minimise total badness (Knuth–Plass), with UAX#14 deciding which breaks are legal at all. Output is locked by golden snapshots, so regressions show up as diffs.
home.pipe.s3.p: Paragraph caches reflow only the dirty interval; breaks settle in background passes. p95 incremental reflow under 8 ms. Output: a display list both renderers draw from.
home.pipe.s3.figAria: Dirty-interval reflow into a display list
home.theatre.p: Knuth–Plass picks break points that minimise total badness across the paragraph — not one greedy line at a time. Red ticks are accepted breaks; the figure is that line's badness (0 = perfect). Hover any line to inspect it.
home.theatre.words: A single Office file holds thousands of declarations: every declaration the engine didn't touch, every ZIP entry, every byte comes back exactly as it was on write-back. The browser tab and the desktop share one layout core: the same shaped advances, the same optimal breaks, the same display list. One keystroke reflows the dirty interval, not the whole document.
home.evidence.s1lbl: real-world corpus files round-trip byte-identical in CI — ZIP64 and unknown extensions included
home.evidence.s2lbl: the same gates run on ubuntu and Windows, each building native + wasm32-unknown-unknown (a macOS job exists but is paused for now)
home.evidence.s3lbl: gzipped first wasm payload — the size budget is a CI gate; CRDT collaboration code lives in a deferred chunk
home.lab.sub: A feel for what reflow costs: the text here is laid out by CSS, not the engine — the point is the interaction, not the numbers.
home.lab.text: An Office file is a container of thousands of declarations. Every declaration the engine didn't touch, every ZIP entry, every byte comes back unchanged on write-back; roundtrip --check verifies this file by file. The browser tab and the desktop share one layout core: the same shaped advances, the same optimal breaks, the same display list — the two can't come up with different answers.
home.formats.h2: One lossless core, three document formats
home.formats.docx.p: Lossless round-trip plus the line-breaking and pagination pipeline — everything the playground runs on.
home.formats.xlsx.p: Same OPC/lossless layer as DOCX. Workbook model and cell parsing come first; formula engine after.
home.formats.pptx.p: Slide and shape model reusing the layout and shaping crates; its own presentation render list.
home.formats.odf.p: ODT renders today — upload one in the playground and it lays out in-browser from content.xml and styles.xml, mapped from the OASIS spec, not from DOCX. ODS and ODP follow.
home.formats.shared: Shared between them: the container handling and the byte-level round-trip guarantees. Not shared: the layout model — DOCX flows, XLSX grids, PPTX places boxes, ODT flows against the OASIS schema.
home.ci.r1p: The ZIP layer copies entries it didn't modify byte-for-byte; roundtrip --check diffs that against a 399-file corpus on every commit.
home.ci.r2p: The engine compiles to native and wasm32-unknown-unknown. The browser shell is a thin platform adapter, not a second implementation.
home.ci.r3p: Format crates never import shells; shells enter through one engine API. check-layering.sh runs in CI, so the boundary doesn't depend on review memory.
home.ci.r4p: Shaped advances against real font metrics, Knuth-Plass optimal breaks, incremental pagination with p95 reflow under 8 ms (benchmarked in-repo).
home.today.p: The engine is licensed Apache-2.0 and the repository is currently private: the code, the 399-file corpus and the CI gates exist and run, but a public checkout is pending the release decision — write to preview@quireoffice.dev for access. The browser playground is being wired to the wasm build: the drop zone exists but doesn't render yet, and that page says so. A hosted editor is further out — XLSX groundwork and the collaborative layer come first.
roadmap.title: Roadmap — Quire
roadmap.desc: Where DOCX stands today, XLSX and the ODF family in progress on the same container layer, then PPTX. Each format is a sibling crate in one repository.
roadmap.sub: DOCX is what works today. XLSX, PPTX and the ODF family (ODT first) will be additional crates in this same repository, reusing the container and round-trip layer — each with the layout model its format needs.
roadmap.docx.l1: Lossless round-trip: the ZIP layer copies untouched entries byte-for-byte, ZIP64 and unknown extensions included — 399/399 corpus files in CI.
roadmap.docx.l2: Line breaking and pagination: Knuth-Plass optimal breaks, UAX#14 rules, CJK anywhere / Latin at whitespace.
roadmap.docx.l3: Page geometry from sectPr, real font-metric shaping, golden break-point snapshots.
roadmap.docx.l4: Incremental pagination with budgeted background reflow; incremental results are checked against full rebuilds.
roadmap.docx.l5: Tables with cross-page slicing, headers/footers with field substitution, style cascade, image placeholders and floating images, forced page breaks.
roadmap.docx.l6: Style-level forced breaks: page-break properties now resolve through both the paragraph-style and direct-paragraph cascade levels — style-level pageBreakBefore no longer drops.
roadmap.docx.r1: Engine foundation — lossless ZIP layer, Knuth-Plass + UAX#14 line breaking, font-metric shaping, incremental reflow
roadmap.docx.r2: 400-file DOCX corpus and round-trip gate (399/399 byte-identical in CI)
roadmap.docx.r3: Cross-page table slicing with repeated headers
roadmap.docx.r4: Headers/footers, section inheritance and PAGE field substitution
roadmap.docx.r5: Style cascade, per-paragraph measure and tab stops
roadmap.docx.r6: Forced page breaks through the pagination chain
roadmap.docx.r7: Image geometry placeholders and floating anchors
roadmap.docx.r8: Floating VML shapes with absolute page positioning
roadmap.docx.r9: 8f4942c Style-level pageBreakBefore enters the cascade (fdo81492, aligned to LibreOffice ground truth)
roadmap.xlsx.l1: A sibling crate (core/xlsx) on the same OPC container and round-trip gates — an 80-file XLSX corpus with per-file licensing is already collected.
roadmap.xlsx.l2: Workbook model, cell projection (five value types) and the style cascade are live on the lossless layer; the formula engine is next.
roadmap.xlsx.l3: Charts come after the grid works, not before.
roadmap.xlsx.r1: 80-file XLSX corpus with licensing and verification gate
roadmap.xlsx.r2: core/xlsx crate, 80/80 byte-identical round-trip, minimal workbook read
roadmap.depth.l1: Tracked changes, columns (w:cols) and the remaining rendering gaps — each item is picked from the failure clusters the corpus comparison ranks, not from a feature calendar.
roadmap.depth.l2: The CRDT collaborative layer sits behind an adapter slot, so the collaboration dependency loads only when a document is actually shared.
roadmap.pptx.l1: Slide and shape model reusing the layout and shaping crates, with a canvas layout model of its own.
roadmap.pptx.l2: A presentation render list on the same display-list contract the native and browser shells already consume.
roadmap.odf.l1: A core/odf sibling crate on the same lossless OPC-style container — content.xml, styles.xml and meta.xml parsed and replayed byte-for-byte exactly like the OOXML parts.
roadmap.odf.l2: ODT (text) leads, with ODS and ODP following on the same core; each keeps only the layout model its format demands.
roadmap.odf.l3: Honest scope: the container layer and the round-trip discipline carry over, the OOXML part model does not. text:sect and office:styles mean different things than sectPr and w:styles, so the mapping is written from the OASIS spec, not guessed from DOCX.
roadmap.products.h2: The product line on the engine
roadmap.products.l1: Embeddable editor components (quire-editor) — CKEditor-style npm packages split by format (@quire/word, @quire/sheets, @quire/slides) sharing one core runtime: mount into any element or run fullscreen, each package carrying only its own format's wasm. Apache-2.0 across the chain; wasm ships in-package with an optional CDN override. @quire/word leads, gated on the editing API — the next engine milestone.
roadmap.products.l2: Desktop app (quire-desktop, Tauri v2) — the native Rust core behind a thin Tauri shell; no wasm detour, installers for Windows/macOS/Linux.
roadmap.products.l3: Collaboration & storage server (quire-server) — self-hostable, Docker-first single image (SQLite + local disk today, pluggable storage layer), CRDT sync on the same loro backend the browser's collab chunk uses. Apache-2.0 like everything else.
roadmap.split.h2: Shell split, when it makes sense
roadmap.split.note: The shells stay in this repo until one ships its own releases, its licence diverges, or its contributor base diverges. Until then the layering script keeps the boundary clean, so a later split is moving directories rather than rewriting.
pg.title: Playground — Quire
pg.desc: Drop a .docx or .odt and the browser renders it with the same Rust engine, compiled to WebAssembly. Read-only beta running entirely in-tab with pure File API.
pg.h1a: Drop a .docx or .odt. Render it in your browser.
pg.sub: The same Rust core as the CLI, compiled to WebAssembly and running entirely in your tab — no upload, no server, the bytes never leave the page. This beta provides in-browser read-only pagination and Canvas2D rendering.
pg.budget: About 1.84 MB raw (about 1028 KB gzip measured), streamed once when you visit this page and cached by the browser afterwards; no other page on this site contains this WASM payload.
pg.dzTitle: Drop a local .docx or .odt here, or click to choose a file
pg.dzSubLoading: Fetching the WASM engine from this site (about 1.84 MB / 1028 KB gzip)…
pg.privacy: Local File API only: every byte is parsed and laid out inside your browser tab. Nothing is uploaded to any server.
pg.errHint: This engine reports state from the real typesetting pipeline and never claims success it didn't get. Check that the file matches the Office Open XML (DOCX) or OpenDocument (ODT) specification.
pg.metaParas: {n} paragraphs in the document · page width {w} pt · page height {h} pt
pg.spec.inputTd: A local .docx or .odt, read in-tab with the File API. Nothing is uploaded.
pg.spec.engineTd: The shells/web wasm build — compiled for wasm32-unknown-unknown, a thin adapter over the same core the CLI uses, streamed on first load with progress reported.
pg.spec.engineVerTd: {ver} — the WASM bytes this page loads are that release's asset, verified against the sha256 recorded in playground.assets.json (the same value shown in the ready chip above).
pg.spec.outputTd: Line-break points and page splits from the real layout pass: shaped advances against real font metrics, Knuth-Plass breaks, pagination per sectPr geometry.
pg.spec.editingTd: Read-only in beta. Caret placement, text selection, and incremental IME typing reflow are deferred to subsequent releases (the invisible anchor contract is established in the web shell; this beta focuses strictly on faithful page rendering).
pg.spec.budgetTd: First wasm payload stays under its budget (~1.84 MB raw, ~1028 KB gzip, cached once on-demand); the collaboration layer is a separate deferred chunk.
pg.status.lead: Read-only Beta is live. The playground now executes the real shells/web WebAssembly engine directly inside your browser tab without any server-side round-trips.
pg.status.corpusP: The layout core is verified file by file in CI against 399 real-world DOCX files, from one-page memos to multi-megabyte technical manuals (including LibreOffice-exported files such as fdo68607.docx); write-back is 100% byte-identical.
pg.status.supportP: Knuth-Plass optimal line breaking, UAX#14 break rules, per-page geometry from sectPr, tables sliced across pages, header/footer field substitution, style cascade (docDefaults → basedOn → direct formatting), image placeholders and forced page breaks (w:br type="page").
pg.status.l1: Read-only rendering: this version has no caret placement, text selection, or incremental IME input.
pg.status.l2: Unsupported layout: multi-column (w:cols) and tracked changes are not implemented yet.
pg.status.l3: Complex graphics: DrawingML vector shapes and SmartArt are known visual gaps, tracked by corpus failure clusters.
pg.status.l4: Font rendering: the browser Canvas2D path uses system/fallback fonts, so there are small visual differences from the native HarfBuzz/swash metrics.

home.bytes.head: The bytes you didn't touch
home.bytes.p1b: is a ZIP of about 20 XML parts plus media. Quire opens it, and the parts it was never asked to change are put back into the new file byte for byte: 399 out of 399 files in the round-trip corpus come back byte-identical to the input, in CI, on every commit.
home.bytes.p2a: That discipline runs the whole way down: the container layer, the
home.bytes.p2b: round-trip tests, the corpus comparison. It is what makes the engine trustworthy for a file you care about.
home.spec.head: How the playground works
home.spec.wasmTd: The engine in the playground is the same Rust core as the CLI, compiled to WebAssembly and running entirely inside your browser tab.
home.spec.nosrvTd: There is no backend in the playground. It uses pure File API and IndexedDB caching, so your document bytes never leave the page.
home.spec.lazyTd: The ~1.84 MB WASM payload is fetched and streamed on demand only on the Playground page. Other pages carry zero WASM overhead.
home.spec.link: Open the playground and drop a file in
home.gallery.aria: Six pages from the round-trip corpus, byte-for-byte identical on save
roadmap.odf.l4: Landed: the 57-file ODT corpus (per-file licensing plus four encrypted synthetic fixtures) and the container-level survey (three spec-violating samples named); the core/odf container crate and the ODT layout projection (headers/footers included) are live in the playground (engine v0.1.0-beta.11), alongside the code-anchored table-model design doc.
roadmap.odf.note: Priority note: the word-family formats (ODT and legacy DOC) now precede PPTX — the editor should cover the most common document formats before presentations.
roadmap.odf.r1: 50-file ODT corpus with licensing and a container-level survey (report-only)
roadmap.odf.r2: ODF design doc fixed and accepted: real code anchors, anchor-gate zeroed
roadmap.odf.r3: 9ccc97c core/odf container crate + ODT layout projection live in the playground (engine v0.1.0-beta.11, anonymous trial)
roadmap.doc.l1: The pre-OOXML binary format lives in an OLE compound file, not OPC — its own parser lane, reusing the same layout and shaping crates downstream.
roadmap.doc.l2: First read-only rendering of real .doc files with untouched-stream preservation; the save path comes after the read model proves out.
roadmap.doc.l3: Honest scope: MS-DOC carries more legacy behaviour than OOXML; expect the schedule to move, and expect the corpus survey to name the gaps before code does.
roadmap.xlsx.r3: Cell-level read projection: sharedStrings, five cell types, sheetData scan — 80-file corpus byte-identical gates untouched
